items.title: 3 big reasons why Black Friday will probably exceed retailer expectations
items.summary:
The Super Bowl for shopping and everything discounts and deals is upon us once again: Black Friday. 

Yahoo Finance Executive Editor Brian Sozzi examines why this year's Black Friday could be a huge event for retailers as US consumers prepare to spend big for the holidays.

items.title: Forget Walmart: Nike Has More to Lose From Vietnam’s Proposed Tariff of Up to 35%
items.summary: Key TakeawaysThe US proposed tariffs on 14 economies, with Vietnam at 20% with a deal or up to 35% without. Nike made about 95% of its brand’s footwear in Vietnam, Indonesia and China in fiscal 2026.

items.title: 3 Dividend Stocks That Could Benefit From the Black Friday Shopping Rush
items.summary: Three retail giants cover their payouts from operating profit and keep raising them, yet each hides a catch that could dent your returns. One carries a sky-high valuation, one leans on refunds that will not repeat, and one faces a margin squeeze.

items.title: U.S. retailers offer Thanksgiving deals even as meal costs, turkey prices rise
items.summary: Investing.com -- Major U.S. companies such as Walmart have been offering Thanksgiving meal kits that are similar to or cheaper than last year’s prices, even as Farm Bureau data showed an uptick in the price of goods for Thanksgiving dinner for the first time since 2022.

items.title: Kroger Just Raised Its Dividend 11% as Shoppers Grow More Price Sensitive
items.summary: Kroger has raised its payout for 20 straight years, but shoppers are filling their carts with fewer items and sales growth has nearly stalled. Can retirees still count on the checks, and which number should they watch next?

items.title: Amazon , Walmart Battle for $124 Billion Holiday Shopping Market
items.summary: Wall Street price targets imply greater upside for Amazon as both retailers expand holiday promotions.

items.title: Amazon Has 59 Buy Ratings and Not a Single Sell. Here’s Where its Headed
items.summary: Wall Street analysts agree on Amazon, yet the stock keeps stalling while AWS accelerates. A $220 billion spending plan and negative free cash flow could decide whether the cloud giant rewards patient investors or tests their nerve.
